verdict.rationale: Daytona documents running shell commands in a sandbox through the SDK (`sandbox.process.exec(...)`), a browser web terminal, and SSH access. Snapshots capture installed packages and dependencies, and you can define packages in an image or Dockerfile, so package installation is supported. missing for 10: an explicit documented example of installing packages at runtime (e.g. pip/apt inside a running sandbox), independent hands-on corroboration of command execution.

support.subject: As a developer, I can run arbitrary shell commands and install packages inside the sandbox

citations.quote: The web terminal allows you to run commands, view files, and debug directly from your browser without installing any local tools.
Daytona provides SSH access to your sandboxes using token-based authentication.
Snapshots are persistent, point-in-time captures of sandbox state, including the filesystem, installed packages, dependencies, and settings.
define the base operating system, language runtimes, packages, and project-level setup in an image or Dockerfile
